items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: Yes, that was Les Hite's band in Los Angeles out of the Cotton Club. I didn't work very long with him. Just for a short time.

ctx.x: they get what they can or what's left over and -- So at that point in those days there weren't many benefits from being --

Oh, no, no, you just paid your dues, and you didn't get anything out of it. At this point I would like to inject one of my favorite recollections. It happened when I was over in Pasadena College. Lionel Hampton and Les Hite came west from Chicago, and one of their first stops was to play a school dance over in Pasadena.

items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: I really can't call names off, you know, quickly.

ctx.x: Yes, we broadcast from the Cotton Club. Oh, we had quite an extensive broadcast. Every night we ran until almost 2:00 o'clock in the morning, from around 10:00 o'clock at night. No pay. But we -- it was just a fine life. That's about all I can say.
Who else was -- worked at the Cotton Club with you, at the same time you were working there with Hite Lionel Hampton and Les Height? About the time you quit.
Gee, I forgot who was in the band. Humph, you know that's almost 50 years ago? I mean, who can remember 50 years? That's pretty hard. I really can't call names off, you know, quickly.
